label: Fused shared experts
mechanism: the two elementwise chains wrapped around the shared sink experts' down GEMM - silu*up*gamma before it, the fp32 expert sum after it - become one Triton kernel each, deleting ~944 MB of HBM per MoE layer that existed only to carry values between elementwise kernels
hypothesis: model.moe_shared is the last bring-up-era eager chain on the MoE block. The routed path has had its epilogues fused since exp-0022 (inter-GEMM silu) and exp-0027 (routing weight + slot reduction), but the n_shared=2 sink experts - present on all 64 MoE layers, in BOTH phases - still run the reference text: silu(gate)*up*g as three elementwise passes over the [S, M, ffn] activation space, and down.float().sum(dim=0).to(bf16) as three more over the [S, M, hidden] output space. At the in-situ cohort shape (M = 4,800 flattened tokens, ffn 3072, hidden 6144, S = 2) that is 413 MB + 885 MB = 1.30 GB of HBM per layer to apply one scalar and add two rows together, against 177 MB + 177 MB fused - ~944 MB per layer of pure inter-kernel carriage, ~60 GB over the 64 MoE layers of one prefill traversal, to produce a 59 MB result. Both replacements are one pass: read the operands the next GEMM already had to be given, do the arithmetic in registers, store once. Independently corroborated by exp-0009's per-layer profile, which priced moe_shared at 0.2 ms/layer at T=736 - ~1.3 ms/layer scaled to the cohort shape, on a layer that now costs ~8 ms total. ONE VARIABLE: kernels/moe_shared.py (new, 2 kernels + 2 wrappers) plus the one call site that reads them, behind PYENGINE_FUSED_SHARED=0, which restores the eager chain verbatim. Nothing else in the traversal moves. Unlike every fused kernel this engine has landed since exp-0013, this one is BITWISE equal to the chain it replaces rather than D13-envelope-covered: aten's CUDA silu on a bf16 input is x/(1+expf(-x)) in fp32 opmath with one bf16 round (Activation.cu silu_kernel - arm 0 confirms the division form, not x*sigmoid(x)), the two multiplies are torch's fp32-opmath bf16 multiplies in Python's left-to-right order, and .float().sum(dim=0) over S = 2 has no reduction order to choose. So there is no accumulated-drift argument to make here and none is made.
predicted_delta: +2.3% to +4.0% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s. Cycle model, built the way exp-0027's was, from the exp-0026 accepted block (609 s box, 2381 requests, 304,768 generated tokens): exp-0017 admits cohorts of 6, so the box holds ~2381/6 = ~397 grouped prefill traversals, each paying this epilogue pair 64 times (every MoE layer; layers 0-1 are dense). At the measured in-situ MIXED-step saving that is 397 x 0.044 = 17.5 s of the box; the decode side adds 304,768/64 = ~4,760 steps x 1.0 ms = ~4.8 s, for S = 22.3 s modelled. CALIBRATION on the two most recent rows measured on these same arms: exp-0025 modelled 64.7 s, delivered +12.4% = 67.1 s actually removed = 1.04x its model; exp-0026 modelled 27.4 s, delivered +2.8% = 16.7 s = 0.61x. Applying that realized/model range [0.61, 1.04] gives S in [13.6, 23.2] s, i.e. 609/(609-S) = +2.3% to +4.0%. The prediction deliberately uses the MIXED step (-44 ms), not the larger PREFILL-only step (-99 ms), because exp-0021's rejection showed the box has far fewer mixed steps than the cohort model assumes while exp-0025's delivered number matched its mixed-step figure. The isolated arm sizes the floor honestly: 0.399 -> 0.064 ms per layer is 21.4 ms of pure kernel time per traversal, and the in-situ prefill step moved -99 ms, so as in exp-0027 the in-situ figure is NOT the isolated arm extrapolated - it also collects the allocator and launch cost of the four deleted intermediates.

local_pregate.lineage: This tree is exp-0027's branch tip (691c6a6) + this one change + a merge of current main, so the row it produces measures exp-0027 AND exp-0028 together; exp-0027's own row was still benching when this was authored and is not yet in the ledger. kill_switch: PYENGINE_FUSED_SHARED=0 restores the eager silu/mul/mul + float/sum/downcast chain verbatim
risks: (a) The decode-side term (-1.0 ms/step) only exists if the CUDA graph is captured with the flag in the state the run uses; the flag is read once from the environment at import in the serving process (the exp-0013 convention), so the server has no toggle race - only the test does, and it handles it by rebuilding the GraphRunner per arm. (b) The mixed-step saving (-44 ms) is the smallest in-situ figure any of the last four fused-chain experiments carried, and exp-0021 was rejected at +0.27% after measuring +124 ms on a mixed step; the difference is that exp-0021's mechanism only paid on MIXED steps, while this one pays on every prefill traversal and every decode step, which is why the prefill-only arm (-99 ms) is reported alongside. (c) Nothing about the GEMMs, the m_cap sizing, the routing or the scheduler moves, so the risk of a surprise is confined to the two new kernels - and both are bitwise-validated against the text they replace at both phases' shapes.
